title: Sunrise City - Neon Echo
text: Bright, major-key synth pop built for morning commutes and getting out of bed. Big singalong chorus, glossy production, relentlessly cheerful. Listeners describe it as a mood-lifter and a good party opener, but it is far too busy to work or study to.

title: Midnight Coding - LoRoom
text: A late night lofi loop with dusty tape hiss, soft rhodes chords and a shuffling boom-bap drum pattern. Popular on study playlists and coding streams because it never demands attention. Warm and slightly sleepy without being sad.

title: Storm Runner - Voltline
text: Driving guitar rock at 152 bpm with a wall of distortion and a shouted hook. High energy from start to finish, with no acoustic instruments anywhere. Frequently used in gym, workout and running playlists. Intense, adrenal, and completely unsuitable for background listening or sleep.

title: Library Rain - Paper Lanterns
text: Rain sounds, muted piano and brushed drums at a very slow tempo. The most acoustic and least intrusive track in the catalog. Reviewers call it the definitive rainy day study record: calm, focused, quietly melancholy but never heavy.

title: Gym Hero - Max Pulse
text: Maximalist pop built for the gym: sidechained bass, huge drops, near zero acoustic content. Energy is pinned at the top from the first bar. Motivating for lifting and cardio, exhausting for anything else.

title: Spacewalk Thoughts - Orbit Bloom
text: Beatless ambient drift at 60 bpm. Long evolving pads, no percussion, almost no melodic movement. Used for sleep, meditation and deep focus work. Calm, spacious, and easy to ignore in the best way.

title: Coffee Shop Stories - Slow Stereo
text: Relaxed acoustic jazz trio with upright bass and brushed snare. Sounds exactly like a quiet cafe on a weekday afternoon. Good for reading, conversation and low key background listening; warm rather than sad.

title: Night Drive Loop - Neon Echo
text: Analog synthwave with a moody arpeggio and gated drums. The archetypal late night driving track: dark, neon, cinematic, propulsive without being aggressive. Not calm enough for studying.

title: Focus Flow - LoRoom
text: Instrumental lofi engineered for concentration: steady loop, no vocals, no dynamic surprises. Slightly more alert than the sleepier lofi cuts. A default pick for deep work and long study sessions.

title: Rooftop Lights - Indigo Parade
text: Indie pop with jangly guitars and a warm, communal chorus. Summer evening music, happy without being saccharine. Works at parties and on road trips; somewhat less polished than mainstream pop.

title: Concrete Kingdom - Vault Kid
text: Hard hitting hip hop with a heavy 808 pattern and the highest danceability in the catalog. Confident, energetic, built for parties and workouts. Lyrics are dense, so it competes with anything you are trying to read or write.

title: Winter Elegy - Aria Sever
text: Solo piano lament, very slow and very quiet, the lowest valence track here. Grief and heartbreak music. Almost entirely acoustic. Listeners either find it cathartic or find it too heavy to sit with.

title: Pulse Machine - Hexadrive
text: Festival EDM with a euphoric supersaw drop at 128 bpm. Purely synthetic, no acoustic content at all. Peak time party and cardio music; there is no quiet section to hide in.

title: Dust Road Memory - Colt Harlow
text: Mid tempo country with pedal steel and an unhurried vocal. Nostalgic, road trip music, comfortable rather than exciting. Sits in the middle of the energy range, which makes it a decent all purpose choice.

title: Iron Verdict - Blacklung Rite
text: Extreme metal at 160 bpm with blast beats and screamed vocals. The most aggressive and highest energy track in the catalog, and the least acoustic. Loved for heavy lifting, hated as background music.

title: Island Time - Sunny Roots
text: Reggae with an offbeat skank and a genuinely sunny disposition, the highest valence song in the catalog. Uplifting and relaxed at the same time. Good for cooking, hanging out, and summer afternoons.

title: Velvet Hours - Mona Skye
text: Slow burn r&b with a smoky vocal and a late night groove. Romantic, intimate, dimly lit. Works for dinner and for winding down; too vocal-forward for concentration.

title: Paper Boats - Willow Hart
text: Fingerpicked acoustic folk, dreamy and soft-edged, almost a lullaby. Very low energy and very acoustic. Reviewers pair it with rainy days, journaling and falling asleep.

title: Listening while studying, reading or doing focused work
text: For studying, reading, homework, coding and deep work, listeners consistently prefer instrumental background music with no vocals, a steady unchanging loop, low to moderate energy, and slow to mid tempo. Lofi, ambient and quiet jazz dominate these study playlists. Lyrics and sudden dynamic changes are the two things that break concentration.

title: Listening while working out
text: Gym, running and cardio playlists favor high energy, fast tempo above 120 bpm, heavy percussion and almost no acoustic texture. Pop, edm, metal, rock and hip hop dominate. Motivation matters more than mood match; sad or slow songs are avoided.

title: Late night driving
text: Night driving playlists want moody, cinematic, mid to high energy music with a steady pulse. Synthwave, moody electronic and darker indie fit. The mood is atmospheric rather than happy, and rarely acoustic.

title: Sleep and winding down
text: Sleep and wind down listening calls for the lowest energy available, slow tempo, acoustic or beatless textures, and no abrupt changes. Ambient, folk and solo piano are the usual choices. Anything danceable is wrong here.

title: Parties and social listening
text: Party playlists prioritize danceability and high valence over any single genre. Pop, edm, hip hop and reggae all work. Energy should stay high and the mood should stay positive; melancholy tracks kill the room.

title: Sad, melancholy and heartbreak listening
text: After a breakup, or when processing sadness generally, listeners look for quiet music with low valence and low energy, often acoustic and often instrumental. Classical piano, folk and slow r&b are common. The goal is company rather than distraction, so a gentle sad song matters more than the genre it belongs to.

title: Rainy day and cozy listening
text: Rainy day playlists overlap heavily with study playlists but skew warmer and slower: lofi with tape hiss, acoustic folk, quiet jazz. High acousticness and low energy are the defining features.

title: What the energy feature means
text: Energy is a 0 to 1 estimate of intensity and activity. Values near 0.3 feel calm, restrained and quiet. Values near 0.9 feel loud, fast and forceful. Energy is about intensity, not about happiness; an intense song can be sad and a calm song can be cheerful.

title: What the valence feature means
text: Valence is a 0 to 1 estimate of musical positivity. High valence sounds happy, cheerful or euphoric. Low valence sounds sad, angry or melancholy. Valence and energy are independent: aggressive metal is high energy and low valence.

title: What the acousticness feature means
text: Acousticness is a 0 to 1 estimate of how likely a recording is to be acoustic rather than electronic. Piano, folk guitar and upright bass push it toward 1. Synthesizers, drum machines and heavy distortion push it toward 0. Listeners who say they want organic, unplugged or warm music are usually asking for high acousticness.

title: What the danceability feature means
text: Danceability combines tempo stability, rhythm strength and beat regularity into a 0 to 1 score. It predicts whether a track is suitable for dancing. It is the single most useful feature for party playlists and is nearly irrelevant for study playlists.

title: What the tempo feature means
text: Tempo is measured in beats per minute. Below 80 bpm feels slow and restful, 90 to 120 bpm feels conversational and mid paced, and above 130 bpm feels fast and urgent. Tempo correlates with energy but they are not the same thing.

title: Known limits of this catalog
text: The catalog contains only eighteen songs. Most genres appear once or twice, so a top five list will usually contain songs from genres the listener did not ask for. Recommendations should be honest about this rather than pretending the catalog is deep.
